_comment: Cursor-format hook bundle, declared by .cursor-plugin/plugin.json's `hooks` field because Cursor's own component discovery defaults to hooks/hooks.json - the CLAUDE-format file, with PascalCase events Cursor cannot read. It runs the SAME scripts as Claude and Codex, never forked copies: hooks/lib/hook-output.sh detects Cursor from the payload (conversation_id / cursor_version / workspace_roots) and speaks {permission, user_message, agent_message} on the tool events; hooks/lib/cursor-output.sh speaks {continue, user_message} on beforeSubmitPrompt, {additional_context} on sessionStart, {pluginPaths} on workspaceOpen and nothing on sessionEnd; hooks/lib/write-targets.py already treats Cursor's `Shell` like `Bash`. Ten of Cursor's 21 events are wired; platforms/cursor/README.md says why each one is, and why each of the other eleven is not. `failClosed: true` marks the safety tier (Cursor's onFailure:block - a crashed guard denies rather than allows); the advisory entries stay fail-open so a broken reminder costs a reminder, not a tool call. The same entries carry `loop_limit: null`, which is most likely a no-op there: Cursor's hooks reference documents `loop_limit` (default 5) only as a per-script limit for stop/subagentStop hooks, not for the permission events these guards run on, and no per-loop cap on a guard was ever measured. hooks/permission-guard.sh (ADR 004 D8) runs on preToolUse (Shell and MCP:<tool> calls) and on beforeShellExecution, failClosed: it answers deny wherever Claude Code would ask, because preToolUse drops an ask and the CLI ignores one under --yolo (S1), except on the desktop app from 3.28.7, where a beforeShellExecution ask is an approval card in every run mode (S2): there it asks on beforeShellExecution and its preToolUse Shell answer is no decision, so that hook is reached. Timeouts are seconds. Measured 2026-09-23 on cursor-agent 2026.07.17-3e2a980 (preToolUse carries tool_name Read/Write/Shell with tool_input.file_path and tool_input.command); desktop >= 3.22/3.24 frames are keyed on Task tool_use_id + child parent_tool_call_id.
